correctness.rationale: A two-sided period-mk word gives an m-by-k array with cyclic column difference equal to the prior column nonzero mask (rotated only at wrap). Telescoping forces every column support weight to be divisible by 3. For m=6 and m=7, all binary masks of allowed weight are exhaustively grouped under rotations and all three additive lifts of each difference mask are enumerated. Each explicit complete quotient graph has only the zero-mask directed cycle, hence no nonzero word fixed by T^(mk) for any k. Two independent graph enumerations and direct state iteration for k=2..9 agree; the proof is uniformly infinite in k.

value.rationale: The object is a recently studied invertible finite-field recurrence with a large family of short cycles at 4k and complicated remaining cycle structure. Excluding both 6k and 7k uniformly (beyond the separate fifth-multiple exclusion) completes a natural three-multiplier gap and shows the 4k structured phenomenon cannot extend to the two neighboring composite/prime multipliers. The short exact mask graph gives a reusable obstruction mechanism and distinguishes period-divisibility from a sample-seed numerical census.
